title: Integration discovery - Cobalt Retail x Redwood
summary: Initial integration discovery focused on how Cobalt Retail would integrate Redwood (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Key concerns: LangChain/LlamaIndex support, running a gateway/proxy in their VPC, rate limiting/quotas per route, observability hooks and token-level cost visibility. Customer wants a pilot and a technical deep-dive benchmarking latency and throughput.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-23
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 36 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood Solutions), Lena (Cobalt Head Eng), Tom (Platform), Aisha (Lead ML), Mark (Security)

00:00 Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. quick intro from our side, I'm Maya, AE. Diego is our SE, Priya is solutions. can we go around real quick?
00:12 Lena (Cobalt): Lena here, head of engineering at Cobalt Retail. we run a multi-tenant platform for order processing and customer support chatflows. Tom and Aisha and Mark with me.
00:20 Tom (Cobalt): Tom, platform eng. we're the infra owners.
00:23 Aisha (Cobalt): Aisha, ML eng. I'm running our embedding and rerank pipeline currently.
00:27 Mark (Cobalt): Mark, security. I might ask a bunch of questions, apologies.
00:30 Diego (Redwood): Great, thanks. goal for today is to understand your integration surface — SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, gateway/proxy options for VPC, rate limit and quota model, and observability hooks you need. We'll cover hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs.
00:45 Lena (Cobalt): Good. our top constraints: latency under 200ms p50 for short chat completions, predictable cost for high volume (we do bursty holiday traffic), and strict data residency — customer PII must never leave our AWS account unless encrypted and auditable.
01:05 Maya (Redwood): Understood. quick qualifier: are you primarily evaluating for customer-facing chat or backend augmentations?
01:10 Aisha (Cobalt): Both. chat assistant is customer-facing, embeddings + rerank is internal search, the search pipeline is latency-sensitive too.
01:18 Diego (Redwood): Cool. on SDKs — Redwood has official SDKs in JS, Python, and a Go beta. they support streaming, chunked responses, function/tool calling. we also maintain LangChain connectors and an official LlamaIndex plugin — the names in the docs are "redwood" and sometimes transcribed as "Redwood Serve" in older samples. they work with recent LangChain and LlamaIndex versions, but if you have a pinned version we can validate.
01:44 Tom (Cobalt): We're heavy on LangChain + the new async chains. how does auth work from a server running inside our VPC to the hosted API?
01:52 Diego (Redwood): For hosted, typically you call the Redwood endpoint over TLS with API keys. If you want to keep traffic inside your VPC, we offer a Private deployment option — control plane with customer-managed networking — or you can run a lightweight gateway/proxy in your VPC that forwards calls to Redwood with mTLS and VPC peering. That gateway also lets you enforce per-route quotas locally.
02:15 Mark (Cobalt): Gateway/proxy sounds interesting. does Redwood provide a reference gateway or do we build our own?
02:20 Priya (Redwood): We have a reference gateway repo — it's a small service (node/go) that handles auth, request shaping, token sampling, and observability hooks. many customers deploy it in their infra and then route from internal services. It supports mTLS and can be configured to cache prefixes and store KV cache locally for same-session performance.
02:38 Aisha (Cobalt): KV cache locally — how consistent is that with Redwood's batching and caching? we're worried about cache invalidation across pods.
02:45 Diego (Redwood): The runtime supports distributed KV cache patterns; the gateway can surface a local in-memory cache for immediate response and forward cache misses. For Dedicated/Private, the runtime has affinity and sticky sessions to reduce cross-pod key churn. cache invalidation is eventually consistent; we can show you the topology during the deep dive.
03:05 Lena (Cobalt): Rate limits — we need per-route and per-customer quotas. we also need burst protection. how are quotas configured?
03:12 Diego (Redwood): We expose rate limiting at multiple layers: API key level, route level, and customer/tenant level. Hosted offers configurable quotas in the console with hard and soft limits, bursts can be allowed up to a configured burst window. Dedicated gives you more deterministic throughput since the capacity is reserved — quotas are simpler to manage there because you control the pool size. You can also enforce proxies to throttle before reaching Redwood.
03:38 Tom (Cobalt): Any hard limits on concurrent streaming connections? during checkout we can have many simultaneous sessions streaming.
03:44 Maya (Redwood): For hosted, there's soft defaults but we can raise limits for accounts; inside Dedicated you set autoscaling policies and connection caps. For streaming we recommend connection pooling and short-lived connections; we can provide client-side SDK patterns for multiplexing streams.
04:05 Mark (Cobalt): Security — SOC2, encryption at rest and in transit, KMS integration for private deployments?
04:11 Priya (Redwood): Yes — Redwood is SOC2-compliant, and Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM for keys. Audit logs and request traces can be exported to your SIEM (we support S3/CloudWatch/Datadog exporters). We'll share the security pack.
04:28 Mark (Cobalt): Data residency again: if we go Hosted, does Redwood persist raw prompts or PII?
04:33 Diego (Redwood): Hosted stores telemetry and logs for debugging but we offer options to redact or disable logging and ingestion on a per-account basis; for full control, Dedicated or Private is recommended. We can sign clauses around data retention for enterprise contracts.
04:50 Aisha (Cobalt): On LangChain integration specifics — do the connectors support streaming tokens to chains and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) workflows?
04:58 Diego (Redwood): Yes, the LangChain connector supports streaming token callbacks and integrates with the retriever APIs — you can plug in your vector store (we work with common ones) and call Redwood embeddings or use your own embeddings. We also have an embeddings-only endpoint optimized for batching.
05:15 Aisha (Cobalt): We use FAISS and an in-house vector store; will there be friction?
05:19 Diego (Redwood): Not really. most customers use our embeddings endpoint and index locally; some push embeddings to us for managed retrieval in Private deployments. For FAISS you can continue as-is and call Redwood for embeddings. we'll demonstrate with LangChain examples.
05:32 Lena (Cobalt): Connectivity: if we run a gateway in our VPC, is there a documented low-latency pattern for calls to hosted Redwood? e.g., keep-alive, regional endpoints?
05:42 Priya (Redwood): We have regional endpoints and recommend colocating the gateway in the same region as your Redwood instance. Keep-alive, DNS pinning, and TLS session reuse help. For the lowest latency we recommend Dedicated in the same cloud region or Private on-prem.
05:59 Tom (Cobalt): Observability hooks — we need token-level cost visibility, per-prompt latency, and tracing that ties back to our request ids. what does Redwood expose?
06:07 Diego (Redwood): Console has token-cost breakdowns (per-request token counts and cost estimate). We emit tracing headers (W3C traceparent compatible) and you can attach your request id header which we surface in logs. We provide webhook sinks for failed requests and a tracing integration for Jaeger/Datadog. There are also per-route dashboards in the console.
06:28 Mark (Cobalt): Is sampling configurable? we can't export every single call to our SIEM; need to sample important requests and send full payloads for only selected ones.
06:35 Priya (Redwood): Yes, sampling rules are configurable — by route, response code, or custom attribute. You can redact PII at source as well.
06:44 Aisha (Cobalt): What about model variants? we want a cheaper fallback for non-critical flows. can Redwood route to a quantized model automatically?
06:52 Diego (Redwood): Yes — smart routing policies can failover to compatible variants (quantized or smaller models). We support automatic fallback and per-route model pinning. You can set a policy: attempt primary model, on latency breach route to cheaper variant.
07:06 Lena (Cobalt): For a pilot, we want to run a few hundred concurrent sessions and measure p50/p95. what's typical setup and turnaround for a pilot?
07:13 Maya (Redwood): Typical pilot is 2-4 weeks: we provision a sandbox account (hosted or dedicated trial), run synthetic load + your sample prompts, collect metrics, and then propose capacity. We'll also do an optional on-prem/Private assessment if you need air-gapped.
07:26 Tom (Cobalt): Do you have connectors or examples for request shaping with LangChain async chains? we've seen TLS timeouts when using naive await patterns.
07:34 Diego (Redwood): Yes, we have patterns in the SDK for async streaming and chunked responses. Example code uses an event-driven callback for token streaming and backpressure support in the connector. We'll share the repo.
07:47 Aisha (Cobalt): Any constraints on prompt size and embedding size? we have long documents.
07:52 Diego (Redwood): Max sequence varies by model; embeddings endpoint supports batching and chunking — we have best-practices for chunking long docs. For very long contexts we recommend retrieval + summarization.
08:04 Mark (Cobalt): Compliance: will you sign a DPA and allow contractual language for data deletion?
08:09 Priya (Redwood): Yes, standard enterprise DPA available. For Private deployments, all data stays in your environment. For Hosted, we can contractually limit retention and provide deletion windows.
08:20 Lena (Cobalt): Costing question — how are embeddings priced vs generation? we need a model to project monthly cost based on our traffic profile.
08:28 Maya (Redwood): Embeddings are priced per embedding unit (per 1k tokens or per vector operation depending on model), generation is per token. We'll send a pricing sheet and a cost-projection template — many customers run a shadow deployment to estimate.
08:42 Tom (Cobalt): Can we set hard budgets per team so dev doesn't blow production budget?
08:46 Diego (Redwood): Yes, per-API-key quotas and per-route budgets with hard caps that return 429 once exceeded. You can also configure alerts and usage notifications.
08:57 Aisha (Cobalt): Observability again — is there a way to surface model regressions tied to prompt sets?
09:02 Priya (Redwood): Redwood Optimize has evaluation hooks: you can register prompt sets and ground-truth checks and get regression alerts when output quality drops. We'll include a quick demo in the technical deep dive.
09:17 Lena (Cobalt): Integration friction — we use internal service mesh; will the gateway/proxy play nicely with service mesh policies?
09:24 Priya (Redwood): The reference gateway is just a service, you can sidecar it or run as a standalone. It emits metrics in prometheus format and meshes with Istio/linkerd. We've seen customers use an Envoy sidecar that enforces mTLS before calls hit the gateway.
09:40 Mark (Cobalt): Incident response — if a model causes bad output or PII leak, what rollback and audit capabilities?
09:46 Diego (Redwood): You can roll back to a prior model version instantly in the console and we keep model versioning and audit logs. For Private deployments you control the image and can revert. We also keep traces for investigations but again retention is configurable.
09:59 Lena (Cobalt): Great. any gotchas about latency when running LangChain with streaming and embeddings?
10:05 Diego (Redwood): Main gotchas: synchronous chaining without streaming backpressure, large batch sizes on embeddings blocking CPU, and not reusing connections. Our SDK examples handle those.
10:18 Aisha (Cobalt): For the pilot, we'd want to test three flows: chat streaming, embedding batch indexing, and rerank pipeline.
10:24 Maya (Redwood): Perfect. we'll prepare sample scripts and a benchmark plan.
10:28 Tom (Cobalt): One more — quotas during holiday bursts: can Dedicated burst into hosted capacity if we exceed our reserved pool?
10:35 Priya (Redwood): Yes — Dedicated supports configurable burst policies into a shared overflow pool (subject to SLA tiers). that gives you predictable baseline with burst headroom.
10:46 Mark (Cobalt): How do we monitor token spend in near-real time? we need for cost-ops.
10:52 Diego (Redwood): Console has near-real-time metrics; we can stream usage to your billing system via webhooks or direct S3 export every 5 minutes.
11:02 Lena (Cobalt): Ok let's recap and confirm next steps.
11:06 Maya (Redwood): Recap: we'll send pricing and comparison, SE will share LangChain/LlamaIndex repo and code examples, Solutions will schedule technical deep dive and benchmarking slot, Cobalt to provide sample prompts and traffic profile.
11:20 Aisha (Cobalt): Sounds good. I'll get the prompt set to you by Sunday.
11:24 Maya (Redwood): Great — thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invites and the pack.
11:30 Meeting end.

Notes on transcript: occasional transcription errors in names (Redwood Serve vs Redwood Server), filler words preserved, some overlap when multiple people talk.
